# Configure authentication to SendGrid

This page shows how to configure SendGrid to enable authentication from Azure Databricks for the SendGrid connector. The SendGrid connector uses a SendGrid API key to ingest data into Azure Databricks. Use the credentials retrieved from the steps on this page to create a Unity Catalog connection in Azure Databricks.

## Prerequisites

- A SendGrid account on a **Pro or Premier** email API plan, or an Advanced Marketing Campaigns plan. Subusers are available only on these plans. For more information, see [Subusers](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/account-and-settings/subusers) in the SendGrid documentation.
- Administrator access to create an API key with read access to the Subusers, IP Access Management, Suppressions, Unsubscribe Groups, Marketing, and Template data.
- To ingest the `contacts`, `lists`, `segments`, `singlesends`, `singlesend_stats`, and `automations_stats` tables, a SendGrid account with [Marketing Campaigns](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/sending-email/marketing-campaigns-overview) enabled.
- If your account has [IP Access Management](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/account-and-settings/ip-access-management) enabled, the Azure Databricks serverless egress IP addresses must be on your allowlist. SendGrid blocks API access from IP addresses that are not on the list.

## Configure SendGrid

Create a SendGrid API key with read access to the APIs for the tables you want to ingest. For more information, see [API keys](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/account-and-settings/api-keys) in the SendGrid documentation.

1. Sign in to the SendGrid application as an administrator.
2. In the left navigation, select **Settings > API Keys**.
3. Click **Create API Key**.
4. Enter a name for the key, then select **Custom Access**.
5. Grant read access to the following permissions, according to the tables you want to ingest. For the API key scope that each permission maps to, see [API key permissions](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/api-key-permissions/api-key-permissions) in the SendGrid documentation.

   | Permission | API key scope | Tables |
   |---|---|---|
   | IP Access Management | Read access | `recent_access_attempts`, `parent_access_attempts` |
   | Subusers | Read access | `subusers`, `recent_access_attempts` |
   | Suppressions | `suppression.read` | `bounces`, `spam_reports`, `global_suppressions`, `blocks`, `invalid_emails` |
   | Unsubscribe Groups | `asm.groups.read` | `suppression_groups`, `suppression_group_members` |
   | Marketing | `marketing.read` | `contacts`, `lists`, `segments`, `singlesends`, `singlesend_stats`, `automations_stats` |
   | Templates | `templates.read` | `templates` |

   Keep each permission category expanded while you make selections. Collapsing a category can reset its selections.
6. Click **Create & View**, then copy the generated key. SendGrid shows the key value only once.
7. Store the key securely. You enter this value as the **API Key** when you create a connection in Azure Databricks. Enter only the key value, without a `Bearer` prefix.

Note the data region of your SendGrid account. EU data-residency accounts use `api.eu.sendgrid.com`; all other accounts use the global endpoint `api.sendgrid.com`. You select this region when you create the connection. The Marketing Campaigns tables (`contacts`, `lists`, `segments`, `singlesends`, `singlesend_stats`, and `automations_stats`) are available only for US-region accounts. Don't select them on a connection that uses the `eu` region.

The API key reads data only for the account it belongs to. To ingest from more than one SendGrid account or subuser, create a separate API key and connection for each.

## Next steps

Create a SendGrid connection in Azure Databricks. See [Create a SendGrid connection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/ingestion/lakeflow-connect/sendgrid-connection).
